handback.t:
The document set is not ready to send: I found 11 must-fix items. Four are model problems an investor will find, three are mislabelled or overstated numbers, and four are honesty issues about the product and how it was built. The full table of every finding is in `C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\bp\factcheck.md`.

**Web checks were limited.** The session had used up its web searches, so I could only open the cited links directly. Carta, ATA and TIA pages were blocked (403), so those figures are unverified, not wrong. I did not check the SSB salary page.

**Must-fix: financial model**
1. **Series A runway.** The Series A calculation runs past month 60, where the model ends. In the downside case only about 13 of the claimed 30 months are actually counted, so "the Series A covers the downside case for 30 months" is unsupported (docs 01 and 02). The base-case need is also understated by about $0.5M, so roughly $6.5M rather than $5.9M.
2. **The downside case is not funded.** It needs $13.35M of seed to reach its milestone at month 47; $5.75M runs out around month 37–38. Neither document says this, and holding back the second tranche makes the gap bigger.
3. **Sales cost ratio.** Doc 04 says the cost model uses the $2.00 of sales and marketing spend per $1 of new ARR benchmark. The model is driven by headcount and implies $0.44–0.76. Meanwhile the 1.7x return on acquisition cost and 36-month payback in doc 02 do use $2.00, so the P&L and the unit economics disagree.
4. **Revenue per account.** At a 25% share, $32K–52K per account means each customer recovers $128K–208K a year. The documents' own examples ($9K, $4K and $9–22K in fees) and the business case (about $13K in fees per account) support only a quarter to a third of that.

**Must-fix: mislabelled numbers**
5. **ATRI detention figures.** $3.6B is ATRI's "unreimbursed expenses during detention" and $11.5B is lost revenue, both for 2023. Neither is unpaid detention or "productivity". The detention market pool ($120–280M) applies a share of owed fees to that expense figure, so it has no valid base.
6. **Charge recognition (158/159).** That is accuracy with no confidence threshold. At the product's actual threshold it recognises 145 of 159 (91%), gets 1 wrong and passes the rest to a reviewer. "Keyword rules (industry standard approach)" is really the product's own earlier keyword rules.
7. **Forecasting methods.** The claim that candlestick-pattern methods were worse than no change is false: in `mkt_bt.out` the pattern model beat no change (0.69 and 0.87 of its error). Only the nearest-pattern method was worse.

**Must-fix: honesty about the product and how it was built**
8. **The "31 held-out engineering tasks" result** (29% fewer tokens, 32% less time, 57% fewer tool calls). In `neural-mesh/bench/codemem/README.md` these are 31 "find the file and line" questions run on one small model. The same README says the component fires on 0.4% of real prompts and that nothing was installed, so "this is how the product was built" is not supported.
9. **"Independent" reviewers.** The "independent" security reviewer, test author and final reviewer are AI agents. No human third-party review or penetration test has been done, and the documents should say so (docs 01 and 05).
10. **Use-of-funds label.** The Series A "Reserve (20% buffer) $3.09M" is 63% of net burn, not 20% (the full table grades this should-fix).
11. **Test count.** "More than 2,000 automated tests in the latest full run" is not supported. That run passed 1,648 tests and found 5 failures, which were fixed and passed a targeted re-run. Unit tests were not part of it. Doc 05's chart has the same problem.

**Should-fix (main items)**
- **Model gaps:** churn has no effect in the model, and "close to break-even in year 6" is beyond the five modelled years.
- **0% bars:** the forecast chart shows 0% where every method was actually worse than no change.
- **Citations that don't hold the cited fact:** the FMCSA source has neither 339,220 carriers nor the 91% figure, and the +0.4% 2025 truckload margin is not in the cited ATRI article. The doc 04 Greenscreens link is a 2022 funding article, not the Triumph acquisition.
- **Other source issues:** Freehand was founded by former Pando executives rather than being renamed from Pando. The Part 541 rules should cite 541.5 and 541.7, not 541.6. The PitchBook $42.4M/$78M Series A valuations are not on the cited page, which only says AI is "roughly double".
- **VC challenges:** the seed is about twice the median round size for a company with no pilots. The section presenting the company as an "AI engineering platform" pulls attention from the freight product.

**What checked out**
- **Model reproduction:** every scenario table, the gate months (47/33/27), the seed and Series A needs, the sensitivity table, team sizes and the use-of-funds splits match `model.py` when re-run.
- **External facts:** FMC $15.4B, ATRI 39.3%/75%/55% and 36–46%, CSCMP $2.58T/8.7%/64.4%, ATRI fuel $0.48 of $2.34, the Cass FY2025 figures, the Loop $95M Series C, the 541.4 court ruling (23 Sep 2025), BLS $135,980 and $124,900, the 14.1% employer tax, BLS benefits at 30.0%, Benchmarkit $2.00 and 77% (2024 data), the WaveUp seed medians, and the Freehand, HappyRobot, Terminal49 and Freightos numbers.
- **Product figures:** the Maersk $3,910 and Hapag-Lloyd $2,550/$2,850 worked examples, the 2,132-case parity check, the 3,000 random invoices, and the security review counts (2 medium, 3 low).
- **Traction:** the "no customers, pilots or deployments" disclosure is consistent across the documents.

The A/B/C source grades are generally fair; the problems are in how three sources are used, not in their grades.
